analysis.investment_thesis: Crompton is a legitimate Indian consumer electrical franchise with a recognisable brand in fans and pumps, an admirably clean balance sheet (D/E 0.05, down from 1.17 in FY22 post the Butterfly acquisition), and ROE comfortably above my 15% hurdle. At 34x PE with wafer-thin 8% operating margins and single-digit earnings growth, the price demands more than the business currently delivers.
key_strengths: Nearly debt-free balance sheet — borrowings collapsed from INR 1,686 Cr (FY22) to INR 186 Cr (FY25), showing disciplined post-acquisition deleveraging
ROE of 17.4% and ROCE of 19% both clear my minimum thresholds; OCF positive all 5 years with FCF averaging ~INR 650 Cr
Steady revenue growth of 9.8% CAGR over 7 years with DII holding 65.7% reflecting institutional confidence in the franchise
key_risks: Operating margins of 7.99% are thin — a commodity input spike or pricing war can quickly turn operating leverage negative
Net profit has been volatile and below 2021 peak levels (617 Cr in FY21 → 442 Cr in FY24 → 564 Cr in FY25), questioning the durability of earnings
Intense competition from Havells, Orient, and Bajaj limits pricing power and constrains margin expansion
red_flags: Finance costs surged to INR 109 Cr in FY23 post-acquisition, masking underlying earnings quality for two years
Butterfly Gandhimathi integration has not yet delivered clear margin accretion — the consumer appliances segment remains margin dilutive
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Crompton's core ceiling fan and pump franchise has real, if moderate, brand loyalty across India's tier-2 and tier-3 markets. The balance sheet transformation is impressive — management prioritised debt repayment and now carries just INR 186 Cr in borrowings against INR 3,270 Cr of reserves. ROE of 17.4%, consistent cash generation, and 9.8% revenue CAGR over seven years paint a picture of a competent, asset-light consumer business.

The problem is margin thinness and valuation. At 8% operating margins, this is not a business with durable pricing power — it is a volume-driven franchise sensitive to raw material costs. Net profit of INR 564 Cr in FY25 implies a P/E of 34x, which I find difficult to justify when earnings growth has averaged only ~8% and the Butterfly integration is still diluting returns. I would revisit this business around 25x earnings.
